new_external_findings.source: Instruct-FD: Can Your Full-Duplex Speech System Follow Turn-Taking Instructions?
new_external_findings.finding: Across six evaluated full-duplex systems, the reported best instruction-conditioned turn-management adherence is 64.4 percent; proactive backchanneling and interruption remain especially difficult.
new_external_findings.f2_relevance: Do not delegate Frankenstein turn authority to an unconstrained speech model. Keep WAIT/backchannel/interruption/cancellation as explicit measurable policy with packet-level acceptance tests even when a native full-duplex model is later used as a signal producer.

new_external_findings.source: Multi-Faceted Interactivity Alignment in Full-Duplex Speech Models
new_external_findings.finding: The work separates interaction behavior into pause handling, turn-taking, backchanneling and user interruption, and reports that explicit axis-specific optimization improves these behaviors on tested full-duplex models.
new_external_findings.f2_relevance: Use the four axes as orthogonal deterministic packet-cortex fixture classes rather than one opaque conversational score. This aligns with the existing HumDial/micro-turn research while preserving causal attribution.

new_external_findings.finding: The current C++17 implementation uses no ASR, LLM or neural VAD in its turn loop; it separates observed voice activity from floor ownership, uses prosodic cues plus an explicit decision policy, models speaker-to-microphone echo evidence, treats short backchannels differently from floor bids, and records how much agent output was actually heard after interruption.
new_external_findings.f2_relevance: High-value bounded donor for pause-vs-gap, backchannel, echo-evidence and heard-prefix semantics. It must not become a second dialogue/effect authority, and its upstream live behavior is not F2 runtime evidence.

new_external_findings.source: BayLing-Duplex: Native Full-Duplex Speech Dialogue with a Single Autoregressive LLM
new_external_findings.finding: BayLing-Duplex represents user speech, assistant text and assistant speech in one interleaved autoregressive path and reports 92 percent turn-taking success and 100 percent interruption success on InstructS2S-Eval. The released inference stack depends on BayLing weights plus GLM-4-Voice tokenizer/decoder components and custom Python model code; real-time use is stated as GPU-oriented.
new_external_findings.f2_relevance: Architecture watch only. German conversational quality, whole-Frankenstein resource fit, local security/runtime audit and authority-boundary integration remain unverified. Do not dispatch while cortex-first throttle is active absent a unique blocker.
